subject: FleetBridge: replacement economics, TCO recapture and handoff
messages:
From: Alex Rios <alex.rios@fleetbridge.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: FleetBridge Procurement <procurement@fleetbridge.io>
Date: 2026-06-30T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood pricing match request for FleetBridge renewal

Jonas —

Quick note from procurement: our current vendor (ScaleServe) sent a renewal that beats our current unit economics. We’re evaluating replacement options ahead of our Sept renewal and want to understand whether Redwood can match/beat the blended TCO when factoring in migration and run costs. Key points:
- Current contract: ScaleServe, $1.2M ARR, committed for 12 months if we sign renewal.
- They are offering a 28% effective discount through a three-year prepay bundle + $120k onboarding credit.
- We care about per-inference unit price, predictable latency, and a clean carrier-grade SLO for production.

Can you share a structured comparison (TCO bridge) showing what it would take for Redwood to be cost-neutral in year-1 and what one-time onboarding/migration credits you’d offer? Procurement attached their renewal quote for reference.

Thanks —
Alex Rios
Head of Cloud Services, FleetBridge
alex.rios@fleetbridge.io

Attachments: ScaleServe_renewal_quote.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rios <alex.rios@fleetbridge.io>, FleetBridge Procurement <procurement@fleetbridge.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing match request for FleetBridge renewal

Alex — thanks for the details and for sharing the renewal quote. We can absolutely put together a TCO bridge that compares: list-price (Redwood hosted), a dedicated capacity scenario, and an apples-to-apples bundle that mirrors ScaleServe’s prepay mechanics. Quick notes / ask list so we model properly:
1) Usage profile (monthly token/embedding volumes by API route; 99th and average seq lengths).
2) Typical concurrency and peak windows (to size dedicated pools).
3) Any egress or data-residency billing considerations.

What we can offer up front: a preliminary TCO workbook and an options-based playbook (credits vs. discount mixed approach). I’m attaching a template TCO workbook — if you can drop metrics in the left column I’ll run three scenarios and a recommended concession structure (migration credit, staged volume-based discount, 90‑day pilot with reduced per-token).

Proposed next steps:
- You drop the usage numbers into RBW_TCO_recap_template.xlsx today or tomorrow.
- I’ll run the scenarios and share a short two-page summary and a recommended commercial package by Thu EOD.
- If that looks good we can lock a pilot and a signed MOU for a 12-month term.

Happy to take a 20‑minute call to clarify anything.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0129

Attachments: RBW_TCO_recap_template.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FleetBridge pricing match — concession guidance

Jonas — looping in Ben on legal/finance constraints. High-level concession framework we can approve (subject to ARR thresholds and PS validation):

- Commercial: up to 30% effective concession in Y1 if the customer commits to a 12-month purchased capacity (blended across hosted + dedicated). We should package this as: 15% baseline discount + an additional 10% volume tier kickoff credit + a 5% loyalty rebate tied to renewal.
- One-time migration credit: up to $75k (covers data export, small infra connectors, and runbook handoff).
- Pilot: 6-week pilot at 50% list with a $0 onboarding mini‑credit to validate perf/latency. Pilot must be limited to non-prod tenant and capped at 250k inference units.
- SLA: can match 99.9% uptime for critical routes; deeper SLOs require Dedicated and an SLA addendum.

Operational notes: ensure we document expected prefix cache benefits in the workbook — FleetBridge’s LLM patterns tend to surface big KV cache tail wins which lower effective token costs. Also add a clause about model fallback (we'll allow an automatic fallback to a smaller variant during capacity stress, with prior notice).

Attached a quick concessions grid to help you assemble the customer-facing offer. Keep the first email to the customer concise; save the full concession logic for the signed MOU.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: concession_grid_q2.pdf

Subject: Revised Redwood offer and TCO bridge — FleetBridge

Alex / Procurement team — thanks for the fast turnaround on the usage numbers. I’ve attached a short summary and a formal offer; below is the customer-facing package we believe is the lowest-friction way to be cost‑neutral to your ScaleServe renewal in year‑1 while preserving performance and predictability.

Summary offer (high level):
- Term: 12 months (option to extend).
- Effective year-1 economics: 25% volume-based discount across API routes (staged: 10% on month 1-3, 25% months 4-12 after threshold).
- Migration/onboarding credit: $75,000 applied to professional services and egress costs.
- Pilot: 6‑week pilot at 50% list for non-prod (capped at 250k inference units).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for specified production routes; Dedicated option available for deeper SLOs.
- Operational: We’ll supply the TCO bridge (attached) showing run-rate parity; we also include a short runbook and knowledge-transfer sessions (3x 2‑hour workshops).

Attached files: redwood-offer-fleetbridge-20260702.pdf (formal term sheet) and tco-bridge-summary.xlsx (detailed numbers and assumptions). If procurement is comfortable we can convert the term sheet into DocuSign and kick off PS within 7 business days.

Please confirm acceptance or let me know one specific commercial ask to reconcile (e.g., larger migration credit in exchange for a 24-month commit). If helpful, I can schedule a 30‑minute handoff with our Solution Architect and PS lead to cover the migration plan next week.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.
